metadata.note: Savannah and Atlanta Railway and its predecessors, Savannah - Springfield - Newington - Sylvania - Millhaven - Waynesboro - St. Clair - Wrens - Camak, Georgia (Fowler route 121, 144.7 mi). Brinson Railway (first passenger train 27 May 1907; built in stages to Waynesboro 1911 and St. Clair 1913) -> Savannah and Northwestern (renamed March 1914, Imbrie interests) -> Savannah and Atlanta (incorporated Dec 1915, built St. Clair - Camak Aug 1916, absorbed the S&NW 16 July 1917). Central of Georgia control from 1951 was a stock purchase only - the S&A kept its own officers and trains, so no Rule 4 split. Drawn exactly the report's drawable spans, with mid-year handovers split so no year is drawn under two operators: Brinson 1907/1910/1911/1912 - 1913 by section, S&NW 1914-1916, S&A Savannah - Waynesboro 1917-1959 and Waynesboro - Camak 1917-1919 [OPEN]. Not drawn: Brinson Waynesboro - St. Clair (track date only), S&NW over St. Clair - Camak Aug 1916 - July 1917 (no passenger evidence), the Savannah Valley Railroad Egypt - Newington stub and the Port Wentworth branch (no passenger evidence), all freight after 1959 (Rule 1), and Central of Georgia trains over S&A rails Ardmore - Savannah 1962-1971 (they belong to the Central of Georgia Nancy Hanks layer, which this layer does not edit). Colours #8B2252 (S&A), #3D6B2F (S&NW) and #AD6A00 (Brinson) are new to the dataset.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] Waynesboro - Camak passenger end: drawn to 1919, the last confirmed year (Fowler 1919w); the real end is later and undated - any 1920s-1940s Official Guide S&A table would settle it. (2) The 1959 end of Savannah - Waynesboro is second-hand (Wikipedia citing the Apr and Dec 1959 Guides); month not established. (3) Brinson-era passenger starts at Newington, Sylvania and Waynesboro rest on track dates (collapsed one year inward), not dated trains; True Citizen Aug 1911 and Sylvania Telephone 1907-1911 not read. (4) Whether the S&NW carried passengers beyond Waynesboro 1914-1917. (5) Camak arrival: Effingham Herald 1913 vs Poor's 1923/railga Aug 1916 - recorded, Poor's followed. (6) Whether the Savannah Valley Railroad ever ran passengers. (7) Mileage conflict: Fowler 144.7 to Camak vs railga/Hawkins 141-143. (8) All headways are estimates; frequencies before 1951 unknown.

segments.note: Savannah and Atlanta passenger trains, Savannah - Port Wentworth Jn - Springfield - Newington - Sylvania - Hiltonia - Millhaven - Sardis - Waynesboro. Starts 1917: the S&A absorbed the Savannah and Northwestern on 16 July 1917 (the S&NW feature is drawn to 1916 so the two do not overlap on these rails). The Central of Georgia bought the S&A in 1951 but it kept its own officers, Guide section and trains, so there is no Rule 4 split. Aug 1951 Official Guide (Feb 1952 issue): trains 21/22 'Mixed', Savannah dep 1:30 PM. Ends 1959: a daily-except-Sunday mixed Waynesboro - Savannah is printed in the April 1959 Official Guide and the Dec 1959 Guide lists the S&A as freight service only - both per Wikipedia's citations, not seen directly, so the end falls between April and December 1959. Headway 1440 min is an estimate from the 1951 table (one mixed each way) applied to the whole span; earlier frequencies are not known. Freight continued after 1959; Central abandoned Sylvania - Waynesboro in 1962 and lifted it in 1964.

segments.note: Savannah and Atlanta passenger trains west of Waynesboro: Waynesboro - St. Clair - Wrens - Stapleton - Bastonville - East Warrenton - Camak (Georgia Railroad connection). St. Clair - Camak opened Aug 1916 and was worked by the S&NW under a traffic agreement until July 1917 - that year is not drawn (no passenger evidence). [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1919 only, by Fowler's 1919 working-timetable letter on Harts (mp 133.2), a passenger flag stop. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service west of Waynesboro actually stopped. The Aug 1951 Guide table runs to Camak but its west-end times are lost to OCR and the index daggers Stapleton, Bastonville and Harts as freight-only, suggesting the mixed was cut back to Waynesboro before 1951; by 1959 it ran only Waynesboro - Savannah. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 1440 min is an estimate (one train each way assumed), not a timetable figure. Freight continues today as NS kaolin/aggregate traffic.
